main_text.head: INDEX
main_text.p: ADventus Magorum quan-dò acciderit? non biennium post na-tum Christum. Pag. 153. &c. nec post purificatio-nem Mariæ, sed ante eam. p. 154-156. quod defenditur. p. 158. &c. imò proximè à nato Christo. p. 150. &c. ad-ventus ille conjungitur cum die nati Christi primo: abitus verò in patriam cum tertio. p. 181: 182.

Æra Christi nati vulgaris. au-ctorem habuit Dionysium Ab-batem. p. 2. Dubia ob diffen-sum de mente autoris, an nativitatis, num conceptionis rationem habuerit, natumque putaverit 25 Decem-bris anni Jul. 45? an 46? p. 3, 4. Non ante octavum seculum admissa. p. 2. Non ex traditione accepta, sed ex falsis calculi suppositionibus. p. 4. Eam patres omnes anticipant. p. 5-8. Vera ut habeatur, vulgaris anticipanda non solum unum annum. p. 133. aut biennium, sed ad minimum triennium, quod ex
main_text.l: anno trigesimo primo currente, & ad finem vergente. p.

page.notes: Blue ink underlinings and strokes over several page numbers (for example 154-156, 158, 150, 181: 182, 45, 46, 133) are later marks, not printed; they are not transcribed. "45?" and "46?" are doubtful as to the question marks and spacing. The decorated initials A and Æ are read as ADventus and Æra. The entry in "acciderit?" has a gap before the question mark, which I have kept as the closest reading. The second entry runs on beyond this part. Doubtful readings: "Actiaca" (first letter of the italic entry word is unclear, written as printed "Actiaca" with [?]). "quis?" and "? p." are printed question marks, not transcription doubts. The blue marks on the scan are not printed text and are left out.
